tasks.gr11-scientific-racism-t3: Topic: Scientific Racism and Social Darwinism. Cover racial classification in the 18th–19th centuries, Social Darwinism (applying natural selection to societies and races), the eugenics movement, forced sterilisation programs, and how these ideas were used to justify imperialism, segregation, and genocide. Ask Grade 11 learners to analyse sources critically, identify assumptions, trace cause and consequence, and evaluate the impact of ideas.
tasks.gr11-nazism-and-race-t3: Topic: Nazi Racial Ideology and the Holocaust. Cover Aryan supremacy ideology, anti-Semitism, the Nuremberg Laws 1935, Kristallnacht 1938, the escalation to genocide, death camps and the Holocaust, the Nuremberg Trials, and the development of international human rights law. Ask Grade 11 learners to analyse sources, evaluate evidence of atrocity, compare historical interpretations, and write essay responses.
tasks.gr11-segregation-and-apartheid-t3: Topic: Racial Segregation in the USA and Apartheid in South Africa. Cover Jim Crow laws and Plessy v. Ferguson 'separate but equal', the 1948 National Party election and apartheid, Population Registration Act, Group Areas Act, Bantu Education Act, Pass Laws, and a comparison of the two systems. Ask Grade 11 learners to compare sources, identify similarities and differences, and construct structured arguments.
tasks.gr11-resistance-to-racism-t3: Topic: Resistance to Racist Ideology. Cover African American resistance (NAACP, Harlem Renaissance, Montgomery Bus Boycott, Civil Rights Act 1964), anti-apartheid resistance in South Africa (ANC, PAC, BCM, Defiance Campaign, Soweto 1976), international opposition (sanctions, global solidarity), and how racist ideologies were ultimately challenged. Ask Grade 11 learners to analyse sources on resistance, evaluate strategies, and write argumentative essays.
tasks.gr11-afrikaner-nationalism-rise-t3: Topic: The rise of Afrikaner nationalism (Grade 11 History, Term 3, South African case study). Cover the South African War and its effects, poverty and the Carnegie Commission, the Afrikaans language movement, the FAK, the Broederbond, newspapers, economic upliftment (Sanlam, Volkskas, the Reddingsdaadbond) and the civilised labour policy. Use original or paraphrased sources and a balanced tone.
tasks.gr11-afrikaner-nationalism-volk-power-t3: Topic: Defining the Volk and the power of Afrikaner nationalism (Grade 11 History, Term 3). Cover how the Volk was defined (language, religion, history, race), class, education (Christian-National Education), labour (the Rand Revolt) and religion, the National Party victory of 1948, earlier segregation laws (1913, 1936), the effect on Black South Africans, and the different explanations of historians (culture, class, race). Present the views of historians in a balanced way.
